title: Hollywood in 1932: the one club and the film's other stars
summary: He knew only Les Hite's Cotton Club in California, since the band worked ten hours a day, and had little contact with Bing Crosby or the other acts.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: '32, what was happening out in California, jazz-wise, were there any clubs?
There was only one club that I know of and that was out where I was -- Les Hite was playing, that was the Cotton Club.
The Sebastián --
Sebastian's Cotton Club.
Right.
That's the only place that I know of out there at the time, cause we were so busy, at the studio, we put in a lot of hours, almost 10 hours a day out there.
Uh-huh.
And you know Cab being so popular, we didn't have any days off, we got through with that we had to come right on back to work.
What about people like Bing Crosby and Eddie Lang, and those other people who were involved in that same film, did you get together with them at all?
No, we didn't. Bing was very friendly.
Uh-huh.
But the rest of people in the show, we didn't come into any contact.
You would think that someone like Eddie Lang would be very interested in --
Yes, but he wasn't.
He wasn't?
No.
And there were some other bands involved in that film, too.
There were other bands, too, we didn't come in contact with --
Or the Boswell sisters --
We didn't come in contact with them at all.
I guess they were done separately.
All separately done.
